subject: Lighthouse Bank RFI: TAM on-call ladder, handoffs, and holiday coverage
messages:
From: Alice Bryant <alice.bryant@lighthousebank.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@lighthousebank.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI: Clarification on TAM on-call coverage and holiday handoffs

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for sending the initial RFI responses. We have a couple of detailed follow-ups specific to operational coverage:

1) Holidays and bank maintenance windows — can you outline the TAM on-call coverage model for US banking holidays, including shift overlap and escalation latencies? We need clarity on guaranteed response windows for Sev 1 vs Sev 2.

2) Cross-region handoffs — Lighthouse Bank requires a documented handoff process if a TAM needs to transfer ownership across regions (we run failover to eu-west). Can you include the exact steps, who owns the paging, and whether Redwood provides a 24/7 paging service or if that is handled by the customer's SRE via integrations?

3) Audit trails — we will need evidence of past incident comm windows (timestamped) as part of the procurement pack. Is a redacted incident timeline export available?

Can you reply with an operational playbook excerpt and any matrix files you can share? Ideally before our procurement sync on Nov 17.

Regards,
Alice Bryant
Director, Vendor Risk & Ops
Lighthouse Bank

--
Alice Bryant

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Bryant <alice.bryant@lighthousebank.com>
Cc: procurement@lighthousebank.com, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:03:14 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Clarification on TAM on-call coverage and holiday handoffs

Thanks Alice — appreciate the specificity. I can provide a compact operational excerpt and an on-call matrix. Quick answers while we assemble the attachments:

- Holidays: Redwood provides a blended model. Our TAM roster guarantees a 4-hour initial response SLA for Sev 1 incidents during declared US banking holidays; Sev 2 is 8 hours. These windows are contractual for Dedicated and Private customers; hosted accounts can opt-in through a premium support package.

- Shift overlap: we run 30-minute shadow handoffs between on-call rotations, documented in the TAM_oncall_matrix (attached). For multi-day holiday periods we add an extra overlap shift and escalation watcher to reduce latency risk.

- Cross-region handoffs: Redwood operates a regional routing policy. If an incident requires region-to-region escalation, the current TAM initiates a structured handoff (1) open incident ticket in our system, (2) export KV cache/log context snapshot, (3) add accepting TAM and regional SRE to the ticket, (4) confirm ownership transfer in the ticket. Paging can be handled by Redwood (24/7 paging with escalation ladder) or integrated into customer PagerDuty/ServiceNow — we support both.

- Audit trails: we can provide redacted incident timeline exports and tokenized communication logs for procurement review. Those are generated as PDF extracts; I will attach an example and the matrix.

I'll loop in Grace (TAM ops) to confirm the matrix and Aditya (Security) for the audit export handling. Expect the formal packet by Monday EOD.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Strategic Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: TAM_oncall_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), excerpt-playbook.txt

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 14:20:40 -0800
Subject: Re: RFI: Clarification on TAM on-call coverage and holiday handoffs

Adding a few security/compliance constraints we must surface to the customer:

- Audit exports: we provide redacted timelines but must not include full PII or customer secret material. The export contains timestamps, actor (role-level), and action summary. For deeper forensic exports we require an executed DPA addendum and a scoped forensic agreement.

- KV cache snapshots: we cannot share raw model KV caches. We can provide summarized context extracts (prompt/response hashes and metadata) and a certified redaction note.

- Escalation watch: for critical financial customers we recommend enabling our Escalation Watch add-on (adds a second TAM during major maintenance windows). This is billable and shows up as a line-item in Dedicated contracts.

Grace — can you produce the example redacted timeline and the playbook extract for Monday? I will prepare the compliance blurb for the RFI packet.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: RFI: Clarification on TAM on-call coverage and holiday handoffs

Hi Alice — attaching the requested operational artifacts for your procurement packet. Below is a concise excerpt from the playbook and a summary table; the attachments include the full on-call matrix and a redacted incident timeline example.

Playbook excerpt (operational highlights):
- Incident classification: Sev 1 = production-wide outage (loss of inference for >5% of users); Sev 2 = significant functional degradation.
- Initial contact window: 4 hours (Sev 1) / 8 hours (Sev 2) on declared US banking holidays for Dedicated/Private customers with Escalation Watch enabled.
- First responder actions (within initial window): page TAM + designated SRE, capture runbook step 1–3, open incident ticket, begin KV metadata capture (no raw cache).
- Handoff checklist: ticket with summary, timestamped actions, artifacts uploaded to secure customer folder, explicit ownership line ("owned by <name> as of <timestamp>"), confirmation from receiving TAM.

Attached files: TAM_oncall_matrix.xlsx (rotation + overlap windows), redwood-escalation-playbook-v1.pdf (excerpted sections), redacted-incident-timeline-example.pdf.

Related links: internal runbook (read-only) — https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/lighthouse-rfi-appendix

If you need any edits to the text for procurement, I'm happy to adjust language or add the DPA/forensic scoping note inline.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
TAM Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
